skill.name: wordpress-dev
skill.description: WordPress development guidance for themes and plugins, including coding standards, security practices, performance tuning, hooks, template hierarchy, and scaffold templates.
skill.summary: Build WordPress themes and plugins with secure patterns, performance guidance, and reusable boilerplate.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many risky-looking patterns, but review found they are Markdown examples, WordPress templates, plugin reference links, and an explicit scaffold generator. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden network callback, or malicious persistence intent was found in the reviewed evidence.

remediation.issue: Absolute scaffold path in usage examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace /root/.claude/skills/wordpress-dev paths with a relative or placeholder path so users do not copy environment-specific filesystem locations.

remediation.issue: Cron example can affect host scheduling if copied without review
remediation.suggestion: Add a note that users should only install the cron entry on systems they administer and should adapt the URL to their own site.

content.user_title: Build Safer WordPress Plugins and Themes
content.value_statement: WordPress projects need secure patterns, fast queries, and consistent structure. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical guidance and templates for theme and plugin development.
actual_capabilities: Explains WordPress coding standards for PHP, JavaScript, and CSS.
Provides guidance for custom post types, taxonomies, hooks, filters, and template hierarchy.
Shows secure WordPress patterns for sanitization, escaping, nonces, capabilities, and prepared SQL.
Includes performance guidance for caching, optimized queries, assets, images, and cron behavior.
Provides reusable templates for post types, taxonomies, meta boxes, REST endpoints, and plugin skeletons.
Includes a scaffold script that can generate boilerplate files from local templates.
limitations: It does not replace testing in a real WordPress installation.
Generated boilerplate still needs project-specific review and naming changes.
Plugin recommendations may become outdated as the WordPress ecosystem changes.
It does not automatically validate compatibility with every theme, plugin, or hosting environment.

use_cases.title: Create a plugin foundation
use_cases.description: Generate and adapt boilerplate for a custom plugin, REST endpoint, or admin meta box.

use_cases.title: Review theme security
use_cases.description: Check theme code for missing sanitization, escaping, nonce validation, and capability checks.

use_cases.title: Improve site performance
use_cases.description: Apply caching, query, asset loading, image, and cron guidance to reduce WordPress overhead.

prompt_templates.title: Start a custom post type
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wordpress-dev skill to create a custom post type for events. Include labels, supports, rewrite settings, and security-safe naming.

prompt_templates.title: Review a form handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wordpress-dev security guidance to review this WordPress form handler. Identify missing sanitization, escaping, nonce checks, and capability checks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a slow query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wordpress-dev performance guidance to optimize this WP_Query pattern. Suggest caching, indexes, pagination, and safer query arguments.

prompt_templates.title: Design a plugin architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wordpress-dev templates and standards to plan a small WordPress plugin with custom post types, taxonomies, meta boxes, REST routes, and asset loading.

output_examples.input: Create a property custom post type for a real estate site.
output: A prefixed registration plan for the property post type.
Recommended labels, supports, rewrite settings, and admin columns.
Security notes for capabilities, escaping, and translation-ready strings.

output_examples.input: Review this AJAX callback for security.
output: A checklist of nonce, capability, sanitization, and escaping issues.
Concrete WordPress API replacements for unsafe patterns.
A short explanation of the remaining manual tests.

output_examples.input: Improve performance for this theme asset loading.
output: Recommendations for enqueue dependencies, versioning, and footer loading.
Notes about what to verify in a browser and production-like environment.

best_practices: Ask for security checks whenever generated code handles user input or permissions.
Adapt placeholder names, text domains, routes, and capabilities before using templates.
Test generated WordPress code in a local site before deploying it.
anti_patterns: Do not paste boilerplate into production without reviewing permissions and nonces.
Do not hard-code project-specific URLs, paths, or text domains from examples.
Do not treat plugin recommendations as a substitute for current compatibility research.

faq.question: Can this skill generate complete WordPress plugins?
faq.answer: It provides plugin skeletons and component templates. You still need to adapt, test, and package the final plugin.

faq.question: Does it focus on classic themes or block themes?
faq.answer: It covers both traditional WordPress development patterns and WordPress 6.x block theme notes.

faq.question: Can it help with WordPress security reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for sanitization, escaping, nonces, capability checks, SQL safety, uploads, and AJAX handlers.

faq.question: Does it run code automatically?
faq.answer: The skill includes a local scaffold script, but usage is explicit. Generated files should be reviewed before inclusion.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude Code support, and the skill is designed for local coding workflows.

faq.question: Are the recommended plugins always current?
faq.answer: No. Treat plugin recommendations as a starting point and verify current maintenance, compatibility, and licensing.
